correctness.rationale: Every normalized open-chain eigenmode has exact parameter QFI theta^{-2}Var(j), because differentiating each amplitude gives (j-mean j)/(2theta) times the amplitude. At theta=exp(u/(N+1)) fixed-u limits reduce to e^{uy}sin²(pi my) for fixed edge mode m and tilted uniform e^{uy} for all indices whose distance from both spectrum edges tends to infinity; the oscillatory weighted sum has a uniform O(1/r_N) bound by Abel summation. Partition integrals and their twice-differentiated logarithms give V_m=Vinf+2(u²-(2pi m)²)/(u²+(2pi m)²)². A one-variable strict derivative inequality shows m=1 uniquely dominates all other finite modes if |u|>2pi; otherwise diverging modes attain the limiting optimum, proving the threshold. A subsequence argument upgrades this to eventual exact endpoint argmax for |u|>2pi and divergence of every argmax below. Replayed verify.py yields 2716 independent finite diagnostic comparisons. The equality regime has no claimed finite-size optimizer.

originality.rationale: The specific new proposition is a sharp optimization and selection transition across all normalized right-eigenstate modes in a critical N^{-1} bias window. Sarkar et al. (2024) Appendix C already derives these eigenstates, a general finite-m mode-dependent QFI expression, and quadratic scaling, so none of that is claimed anew. Liu et al. (2026) independently prove optimal position measurement for real-amplitude states and apply it to the same eigenstates; they do not state or prove the sharp mode switch. Wiersig–Rotter (2026) use QFI of scattering outputs, which does not subsume this single-right-eigenstate normalized-chain optimization. Exact semantic searches of published results yielded no same-object crossover or equivalent statement. The 2024 general expression makes the numerical answer derivable in principle, but does not state the all-mode optimization (including diverging indices), nor the eventual exact extremal mode selection. Residual risk: possible earlier implicit/unindexed derivation.
residual_risks: Although the 2024 Appendix C general formula does not state the optimized phase transition, its sums can be further manipulated to derive this theorem; additional unindexed work may have carried out that optimization.
The 2026 Liu et al. supplementary material was not materially inspected; the examined main article contains no same-object mode-selection result.
The 2026 Wiersig–Rotter manuscript was compared at abstract level because its scattering-matrix objects differ; this is not a full-text exclusion certificate.
External publication priority, independent audit and experimental realism of eigenstate selection have not been established.

value.rationale: The object is a physically motivated sensing eigenfamily: the key design question is which measurable right eigenstate provides the greatest information about the asymmetric hopping ratio at criticality. The exact optimizer is qualitatively different across the explicit |u|=2pi threshold: high/interior modes dominate close to symmetry, whereas m=1 and m=N are eventually the unique exact finite-chain optimizers outside. The result supplies the complete leading Heisenberg-scale constant after maximization over all N modes, including n-dependent frequency choices, rather than a textbook variance computation for a single fixed state or a merely numerical observation. No broad downstream theorem is claimed; omitted preparation costs and equality finite-size effects are explicit boundaries.
